summary: Draft Control Power record. `AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests` sits under `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Power`, has an explicit repo-doc default of `1`, is absent on the observed clean baseline, produced an exact current-build Unicode string hit in `ntoskrnl.exe`, and was later retained by source-enrichment as a docs-first kernel candidate with a `power-request-simulation` trigger recommendation. A later repo-native follow-up then exposed that same trigger family as a named guest Procmon profile and mega-trigger runtime alias. A later KVM local-KD pass then resolved live current-build `nt!PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution = 1`, which aligns with the repo-doc default. A later static INIT-table follow-up then showed a current-build `ntoskrnl.exe` descriptor entry under `Power` that binds `AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests` to the exact global later resolved by local KD as `nt!PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution`. A later current-build disassembly pass then showed direct consumers in `nt!PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate` and `nt!PopPowerRequestCallbackExecutionRequired`. Later follow-ups then showed `nt!PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideQuery` packaging requester state for `nt!PopUmpoSendPowerMessage`, `nt!PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback` staying timeout-setting specific by updating `nt!PopExecutionRequiredTimeout`, the timeout timer/worker chain feeding back into `nt!PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate`, the broader override-response plus callback-worker path staying queue and PDC driven with no visible `*PowerRequest*Reg*` symbol, and a generic power-setting callback subsystem around `PoRegisterPowerSettingCallback` and `PopInitializePowerSettingCallbacks`. A later host-side objdump follow-up then showed an unlabeled current-build `INIT` walker at `0x140C48AB8` uniquely consuming the broader `Power` descriptor table, passing row key and value names through subkey and value-lookup helpers before copying payload into the paired target global. The lane is strong enough for a schema-backed draft, but it still lacks a primary current-build doc and an exact runtime registry read.

setting.name: Allow System Required Power Requests
setting.casual_explanation: This appears to be a kernel-adjacent Control Power setting tied to how the power manager treats system-required power requests. It is being tracked as a research candidate, not a user-facing tweak.
setting.why_people_change_it: Kernel and power researchers may inspect this value when investigating how system-required power requests are converted, honored, or suppressed under undocumented power-policy flows.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The value now has a stronger evidence chain because it has repo docs, observed baseline state, an exact current-build string hit, a retained enrichment recommendation, a repo-native trigger harness, a live current-build KVM local-KD value that matches the repo-doc default, direct current-build consumer disassembly, a visible UMPO override-query lineage, a timeout-setting callback disassembly, a retained timeout timer/worker chain, a retained override-response plus callback-worker follow-up that still exposed no visible `*PowerRequest*Reg*` symbol, a retained generic power-setting callback infrastructure pass around `PoRegisterPowerSettingCallback`, and a later host-side static walker analysis that materially closes the old seeding-path gap. It is still too weak for a published tweak because that seeding path is only statically inferred from current-build disassembly, no primary current-build doc backs it, and an exact runtime registry read remains unresolved.
setting.professional_notes: Repo power docs assign `AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests = 1` under `Control\\Power` and map it to `PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution`. The power routing note later kept the value inside the `Control\\Power` docs cluster. The observed clean baseline then confirmed that the parent `Control\\Power` path exists while the value itself is absent. A later targeted current-build string batch found an exact Unicode hit for `AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests` in `ntoskrnl.exe`, which is stronger than a pure docs-only mention and enough to keep the value out of raw backlog. Source-enrichment later retained the candidate in the canonical queue with `power-request-simulation` as the suggested trigger family, specifically `PowerCreateRequest(SystemRequired)`, `PowerSetRequest(DisplayRequired)`, and an audio playback session. A later repo-native follow-up then exposed that same trigger family as a named guest Procmon profile plus a matching mega-trigger runtime alias, closing the old trigger-design gap before the first dedicated narrow replay. A later KVM local-KD pass then resolved live current-build `nt!PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution = 1`, which matches the repo-doc default and also surfaced the sibling symbol `nt!PopPowerRequestActiveAudioEnablesExecutionRequired` in the same wildcard sweep. A later static INIT-table follow-up then found the exact current-build value-name string in `ntoskrnl.exe`, placed it inside an `INIT` descriptor slice under the shared `Power` key string, and matched the paired target-global pointer to `nt!PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution` via the retained local-KD symbol address. A later current-build disassembly pass then showed direct reads of `nt!PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution` inside `nt!PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate` and `nt!PopPowerRequestCallbackExecutionRequired`, while `nt!PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback` chained into that same reader family through `PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionmentUpdate`. A later wildcard lineage pass then showed that the current build exposes only one `*PowerRequest*Setting*` symbol, `nt!PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback`, alongside `PopPowerRequestInitialize`, `PopPowerRequestOverrideInitialize`, and the `PopExecutionRequiredTimeout` family. A later init/override disassembly pass then showed `PopPowerRequestInitialize` only zeroing per-object fields and `PopPowerRequestOverrideInitialize` iterating `PopPowerRequestObjectList` before calling `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideQuery`, which is useful because it still did not expose a registry read in the visible current-build init path. A later dedicated UMPO disassembly pass then showed `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideQuery` storing requester identity via `PoStoreRequester`, allocating an `Umpo`-tagged buffer, and dispatching `PopUmpoSendPowerMessage`, while wildcard output exposed `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestCreate`, `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestAction`, and `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideCleanup`. A later dedicated callback disassembly pass then showed `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback` comparing the incoming GUID against `GUID_EXECUTION_REQUIRED_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`, requiring a 4-byte payload, writing `PopExecutionRequiredTimeout`, rearming `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredTimeoutTimer`, and then calling `PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate`. A later timeout-lineage pass then showed `PopPowerRequestSetExecutionRequiredTimeoutTimer` reading `PopExecutionRequiredTimeout`, comparing it against `PopExecutionRequiredContext`, and arming `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredTimeoutTimer` via `KeSetTimer2`, while `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredTimeoutCallback` simply queued work and `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredTimeoutWorker` re-entered `PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate`. A later response-lineage follow-up then showed `x nt!*PowerRequest*Reg*` returning no visible current-build symbols, `PopPowerRequestHandleRequestOverrideQueryResponse` updating request state, re-evaluating pending request status, and queueing `PopPowerRequestUpdateWorkItem`, `PopPowerRequestCallbackWorker` draining the update queue through `PopPowerRequestStatsSetActive` and `PopPowerRequestHandleRequestUpdate`, and `PopPowerRequestCallbackExecutionRequired` consulting `PoPdcCallbacks`, updating `PopPowerRequestPdcNotifiedExecutionRequired` or `PopPowerRequestPdcNotifiedSystemRequired`, testing `PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution`, and then writing `PopSIdle` policy state before `PopCheckResiliencyScenarios`. A later power-setting lineage pass then exposed the broader current-build infrastructure around this family: `x nt!*PowerSetting*` returned `PopInitializePowerSettingCallbacks`, `PopInitializePowerSettings`, `PoRegisterPowerSettingCallback`, `PoUnregisterPowerSettingCallback`, `PopDispatchPowerSettingCallbacks`, `PopCallPowerSettingCallback`, `PopQueryPowerSettingUlong`, `PopSetPowerSettingValue`, and `PopRegisteredPowerSettingCallbacks`, while `x nt!*ExecutionRequired*Setting*` still returned only `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback`. The same pass showed `PoRegisterPowerSettingCallback` allocating a callback object, copying the target GUID and callback pointer, and resolving the setting through `PopFindPowerSettingConfiguration`, which is strong proof that the visible execution-required family now sits on a generic power-setting callback subsystem even though the exact binding site for `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback` is still unresolved. This matters because the visible family is now callback/init/timeout-setting/timer-worker/UMPO/override-response/PDC/power-setting-subsystem driven and still does not demonstrate a registry read or a direct write to `PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution`. A later host-side objdump/xref follow-up then narrowed the old seeding gap substantially: an unlabeled `INIT` walker at `0x140C48AB8` uniquely loads the broader `0x140C72E30` `Power` descriptor table, passes each row key string through `0x1407E334C`, each row value name through `0x14086A794` and `0x14086C510`, and the row target pointer through `0x140C4CB20`; this is best read as the current-build static registry seeding path for the execution-required pair even though the routine is not yet symbol-resolved or backed by a primary Microsoft doc. The next proof step is now narrower: symbol-resolve or document that unlabeled init walker, or capture an exact runtime registry read for the value.

evidence.title: Repo power docs assign AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests = 1
evidence.summary: Repo docs assign `AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests = 1` under `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Power` and map it to `PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution`.

evidence.title: Observed baseline existence for AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests
evidence.summary: The observed clean baseline confirmed that `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Power` exists while `AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests` itself is absent.

evidence.title: Current-build string hit for AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests
evidence.summary: The broad current-build string batch found an exact Unicode hit for `AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests` in `C:\\Windows\\System32\\ntoskrnl.exe`.

evidence.title: Source-enrichment keeps AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests as a docs-first kernel candidate with a power-request trigger family
evidence.summary: Source-enrichment kept the value in the canonical queue as a docs-first `Control\\Power` candidate and suggested `power-request-simulation` as the next runtime family, with `PowerCreateRequest(SystemRequired)`, `PowerSetRequest(DisplayRequired)`, and audio playback as concrete trigger primitives.

evidence.title: Repo guest tooling now exposes a named power-request-simulation harness
evidence.summary: The generic Procmon guest tool now exposes `TriggerProfile = power-request-simulation`, and the mega-trigger runtime surface now exposes the matching `power_request_simulation` alias, both using the same `PowerCreateRequest(SystemRequired/DisplayRequired/AwayMode)` primitive family recommended by source-enrichment.

evidence.title: KVM local-KD resolves live PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution = 1
evidence.summary: A retained KVM local-KD pass resolved `nt!PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution` and read its live value as `1`. The same wildcard sweep also resolved the sibling symbol `nt!PopPowerRequestActiveAudioEnablesExecutionRequired`, but did not read its value.

evidence.title: KVM local-KD disassembly shows current-build consumers for PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution
evidence.summary: A retained KVM local-KD disassembly pass showed direct reads of `nt!PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution` in `nt!PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate` and `nt!PopPowerRequestCallbackExecutionRequired`. The same pass also showed `nt!PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback` chaining into `PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionmentUpdate`.

evidence.title: KVM local-KD wildcard pass narrows execution-required setting lineage
evidence.summary: A retained KVM local-KD wildcard pass showed that the current build exposes only one `*PowerRequest*Setting*` symbol, `nt!PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback`, alongside `PopPowerRequestInitialize`, `PopPowerRequestOverrideInitialize`, and the `PopExecutionRequiredTimeout` family. This narrows the visible lineage to callback/init surfaces rather than a demonstrated registry reader.

evidence.title: KVM local-KD disassembly shows init and override path without a visible registry read
evidence.summary: A retained KVM local-KD disassembly pass showed `PopPowerRequestInitialize` only zeroing per-object fields, while `PopPowerRequestOverrideInitialize` iterated `PopPowerRequestObjectList` and called `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideQuery`. The visible init/override path did not expose a registry read.

evidence.title: KVM local-KD disassembly shows UMPO override-query lineage without a visible registry read
evidence.summary: A retained KVM local-KD follow-up showed `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideQuery` calling `PoStoreRequester`, allocating an `Umpo`-tagged buffer, and dispatching `PopUmpoSendPowerMessage`. The same wildcard pass exposed `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestCreate`, `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestAction`, and `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideCleanup`, keeping the visible lineage callback/init/UMPO-query centric rather than registry-backed.

evidence.title: KVM local-KD disassembly shows timeout-setting callback semantics for the execution-required family
evidence.summary: A retained KVM local-KD pass showed `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback` matching `GUID_EXECUTION_REQUIRED_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`, requiring a 4-byte payload, writing `PopExecutionRequiredTimeout`, rearming `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredTimeoutTimer`, and then calling `PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate`. The visible callback is timeout-setting specific rather than a demonstrated registry-backed seeding path for `PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution`.

evidence.title: KVM local-KD disassembly shows execution-required timeout timer and worker lineage
evidence.summary: A retained KVM local-KD pass showed `PopPowerRequestSetExecutionRequiredTimeoutTimer` reading `PopExecutionRequiredTimeout` and arming `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredTimeoutTimer` through `KeSetTimer2`, `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredTimeoutCallback` queueing work with `PopQueueWorkItem`, and `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredTimeoutWorker` re-entering `PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate`. The visible timeout family remains runtime timer/worker driven rather than registry-backed.

evidence.title: KVM local-KD disassembly shows execution-required override-response and callback-worker lineage
evidence.summary: A retained KVM local-KD follow-up showed `x nt!*PowerRequest*Reg*` returning no visible current-build symbols, `PopPowerRequestHandleRequestOverrideQueryResponse` updating request state and queueing `PopPowerRequestUpdateWorkItem`, `PopPowerRequestCallbackWorker` draining the update queue through `PopPowerRequestStatsSetActive` and `PopPowerRequestHandleRequestUpdate`, and `PopPowerRequestCallbackExecutionRequired` consulting `PoPdcCallbacks`, `PopPowerRequestPdcNotified*`, `PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution`, and `PopSIdle`. The visible family remained runtime callback and queue driven rather than registry-backed.

evidence.title: KVM local-KD wildcard pass exposes generic power-setting callback subsystem around the execution-required family
evidence.summary: A retained KVM local-KD wildcard pass showed generic current-build power-setting infrastructure including `PopInitializePowerSettingCallbacks`, `PopInitializePowerSettings`, `PoRegisterPowerSettingCallback`, `PoUnregisterPowerSettingCallback`, `PopDispatchPowerSettingCallbacks`, `PopCallPowerSettingCallback`, `PopQueryPowerSettingUlong`, `PopSetPowerSettingValue`, and `PopRegisteredPowerSettingCallbacks`. The same pass also showed `x nt!*ExecutionRequired*Setting*` still returning only `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback`, while `PoRegisterPowerSettingCallback` allocates a callback object, copies the target GUID and callback pointer, and resolves the backing setting through `PopFindPowerSettingConfiguration`.

evidence.title: Current-build INIT descriptor table binds AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests to PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution
evidence.summary: A retained guest-side UTF-16 scan found the exact current-build value-name string in `ntoskrnl.exe`, and a follow-up host-side table decode showed that the surrounding `INIT` descriptor slice binds the `Power` key plus that value name to the same kernel global later resolved by local KD on the current build.

evidence.title: Host-side objdump follow-up shows a generic INIT walker seeding the execution-required Power row
evidence.summary: A retained host-side disassembly follow-up showed an unlabeled current-build `INIT` routine at `0x140C48AB8` uniquely loading the broader `0x140C72E30` `Power` descriptor table, passing each row key string through a subkey lookup helper, each row value name through a value-name lookup helper, and the row target pointer through a copy helper. This is an inference from current-build disassembly rather than a symbolized Microsoft routine name, but it materially closes the older seeding-path gap for `AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests`.

decision.why: The candidate is strong enough for a schema-backed draft because it has a repo-doc default, observed baseline state, a current-build string hit, a retained enrichment recommendation, a matching repo-native trigger harness, a live KVM local-KD value that aligns with the repo-doc default, direct current-build callback/reader disassembly, a visible UMPO override-query lineage, a timeout-setting callback disassembly, a retained timeout timer/worker chain, a retained override-response plus callback-worker follow-up that still exposed no visible `*PowerRequest*Reg*` symbol, a retained generic power-setting callback subsystem pass around `PoRegisterPowerSettingCallback`, a later current-build INIT-table binding that maps the exact value name to the KD-resolved target global, and a later host-side disassembly follow-up that statically recovers the generic init walker feeding that table. It is not ready for validation because that seeding path is still unlabeled and documentation-light, and an exact runtime registry read remains unresolved.

open_questions: Can the unlabeled current-build `INIT` walker at `0x140C48AB8`, plus its wrappers at `0x140C483EF` and `0x140C48414`, be symbol-resolved or tied to a documented power-init routine?
Does the new repo-native `power-request-simulation` harness surface a narrower exact-read lane for this value?
Is the observed live `1` an unconditional built-in default, or an override only consulted under specific power-request flows?
